competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both named properties are genuinely applied, not merely named, and the keys are right. Zero-identity: seed 43 'Grace solved: "0 + 10 = ___". Grace says the blank is 10.' (has_error false), seed 603 'What is 18 + 0?' -> 18, seed 70 '10 + 0 = ___' -> 10, and seed 604 '7 + 0 = 8. True or False?' correctly False. Order-of-addends: seed 44 'Is 12 + 2 the same as 2 + 12?' -> true and seed 600 'Is 16 + 3 the same as 3 + 16?' -> true, with discriminating non-examples such as seed 602 'Is 13 + 3 the same as 3 + 10?' -> false. The competency's phrasing is 'Illustrate BY applying', so application is the stated mode of illustration and these items satisfy that verb.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both clauses appear and are close to balanced -- 8 zero-identity items (seeds 42, 43, 46, 70, 601, 603, 604, 606) and 7 order items (seeds 44, 45, 500, 501, 502, 600, 602). The gap is in the form of the order clause: every single order item is a yes/no judgement of a pair the item already supplies ('Is 17 + 2 the same as 2 + 17?', seed 45), and not one asks the student to USE the property to produce a value -- no item asks the pupil to reuse a known sum to produce its commuted partner. Every generative item in the packet ('What is 0 + 19?', seed 601; '10 + 0 = ___', seed 70) belongs to the zero clause. So the second property is exercised only in recognition form.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: This is Grade 1, Quarter 1. The seven order-comparison MCQs (seeds 44, 45, 500, 501, 502, 600, 602) all carry the same two verbal distractors, 'Cannot be determined' and 'Only when both are 0'. Both are heavy reading for a first-quarter Grade 1 pupil and neither is a misconception a six-year-old actually holds about 12 + 2 versus 2 + 12, so they add decoding load without diagnostic value. The arithmetic itself is correctly pitched -- seed 42 '1 + 0 = 1. True or False?' and seed 606 'What is 12 + 0?' are exactly right for the level, and those items sensibly use numeric distractors (12, 22, 11, 13) instead.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four formatters appear (true_false at seeds 42 and 604, error_detect at seed 43, cloze at seed 70, mcq for the remaining eleven), but the stems collapse into two templates. Seven items share one comparison template with an identical four-option pool (seeds 44, 45, 500, 501, 502, 600, 602), and four more are bare zero-addend fill-ins (seeds 46, 601, 603, 606). Nothing uses a story context, countable objects, a ten-frame or a number line -- all fifteen items are bare symbolic notation, and the single error_detect item (seed 43) is the only one with a named character.

competency_alignment.rationale: Nothing reaches past the competency. Only two-addend whole-number addition appears: no subtraction, no three-addend sums, no missing-addend algebra, no place-value or regrouping vocabulary. The order items compare exactly two two-term sums, which is literally 'changing the order of the addends' (seed 600 'Is 16 + 3 the same as 3 + 16?'), and the zero items are literally 'the sum of zero and any number' (seed 43 '0 + 10 = ___', seed 603 'What is 18 + 0?').

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every quantity stays inside 'sums up to 20'. The largest sums are seed 502 'Is 13 + 6 the same as 6 + 14?' (19 and 20, the boundary itself), seed 45 '17 + 2' (19), seed 500 'Is 18 + 1 the same as 1 + 14?' (19 and 15), and seed 601 'What is 0 + 19?' (19). No sum exceeds 20 and no addend exceeds 19; distractors stay in range too (seed 70 offers 9, 10, 11, 20).
